notes: This skill's output is almost entirely files on disk, which makes it the best-suited engineering skill for script assertions: nearly every claim is decidable by reading the sandbox. The recurring theme across evals is restraint, and it is where the skill is most likely to slip. Two cases specifically guard against creating Prettier files when Prettier was not chosen: eslint-config-prettier is a compatibility shim that switches off ESLint's formatting rules, so installing it does not mean Prettier is in use, and .prettierrc.json or .prettierignore appearing alongside oxfmt is a real defect. Installs cannot complete (no network), so assertions check declared config and package.json rather than an installed node_modules. Wiring linters into git hooks belongs to git-hooks-setup, so hook artefacts appearing here are also a defect.

evals.name: greenfield-oxlint-oxfmt
evals.prompt: I have a new TypeScript React project with no linting or formatting set up. I want oxlint for linting and oxfmt for formatting. We use npm. Apply the changes directly, you have my go-ahead, please don't stop to ask me to confirm.
evals.expected_output: Creates .oxlintrc.json and .oxfmtrc.json with the skill's default configs, and adds lint and format scripts to package.json pointing at oxlint and oxfmt. No ESLint, Prettier, or Biome config appears, since none was asked for.

assertions.text: Creates .oxlintrc.json
Creates .oxfmtrc.json
The package.json lint script runs oxlint
assertions.script: python3 -c "import json,sys; s=json.load(open('sandbox/package.json')).get('scripts',{}); sys.exit(0 if 'oxlint' in s.get('lint','') else 1)"

assertions.text: The package.json format script runs oxfmt
assertions.script: python3 -c "import json,sys; s=json.load(open('sandbox/package.json')).get('scripts',{}); sys.exit(0 if 'oxfmt' in s.get('format','') else 1)"

assertions.text: Creates no ESLint, Prettier, or Biome config, none of which was requested
assertions.script: ! ls sandbox/eslint.config.js sandbox/.eslintrc* sandbox/biome.json sandbox/.prettierrc* sandbox/.prettierignore >/dev/null 2>&1

assertions.text: Wires nothing into git hooks, that being git-hooks-setup's job

evals.name: partial-add-oxfmt-only
evals.prompt: Our JS/TS project already has oxlint configured. We want to add oxfmt for formatting. We use npm. Apply the changes directly, you have my go-ahead, please don't stop to ask me to confirm.
evals.expected_output: The existing .oxlintrc.json and lint script are detected and left exactly as they are. Only .oxfmtrc.json and a format script are added, since the linting half of the setup is already done and rewriting it would be gratuitous churn.

assertions.text: Creates .oxfmtrc.json
Adds a format script running oxfmt
assertions.script: python3 -c "import json,sys; s=json.load(open('sandbox/package.json')).get('scripts',{}); sys.exit(0 if 'oxfmt' in s.get('format','') else 1)"

assertions.text: Leaves the existing .oxlintrc.json byte-for-byte unchanged
Leaves the existing lint script unchanged
assertions.script: python3 -c "import json,sys; s=json.load(open('sandbox/package.json')).get('scripts',{}); sys.exit(0 if s.get('lint')=='oxlint src' else 1)"

evals.name: multi-ecosystem-go-shell
evals.prompt: Set up linting for our Go server and our shell deployment scripts. Apply the changes directly, you have my go-ahead, please don't stop to ask me to confirm.
evals.expected_output: Creates .golangci.yaml including a formatters block with at least gofmt and goimports, a Makefile with pinned local golangci-lint install and lint targets, and a .shellcheckrc with shell=bash. Nothing JS-related is created, since there is no package.json in this repo at all.

assertions.text: Creates .golangci.yaml
The golangci config includes a formatters block with gofmt and goimports
assertions.script: F=$(ls sandbox/.golangci.y*ml | head -1); grep -q 'formatters' "$F" && grep -q 'gofmt' "$F" && grep -q 'goimports' "$F"

assertions.text: Creates a Makefile with a lint target and a pinned golangci-lint version
assertions.script: test -f sandbox/Makefile && grep -q 'lint' sandbox/Makefile && grep -qE 'GOLANGCI_VERSION|golangci-lint-' sandbox/Makefile

assertions.text: Makefile recipe lines use real tab characters, without which make fails outright
Creates .shellcheckrc specifying bash
Creates no JS tooling, this repo having no package.json

evals.name: mixed-workspace-js-and-go
evals.prompt: Set up oxlint and oxfmt for the JS/TS workspace and golangci-lint for the Go server. We use pnpm. Apply the changes directly, you have my go-ahead, please don't stop to ask me to confirm.
evals.expected_output: Both ecosystems are configured in one pass: .oxlintrc.json and .oxfmtrc.json for the JS workspace with lint and format scripts in package.json, plus .golangci.yaml and a Makefile for the Go server. Install commands use pnpm, matching the packageManager field and the pnpm-workspace.yaml.

assertions.text: Creates both .oxlintrc.json and .oxfmtrc.json for the JS workspace
Creates the golangci config for the Go server
Creates a Makefile with a lint target for the Go side
Adds lint and format scripts to package.json
assertions.script: python3 -c "import json,sys; s=json.load(open('sandbox/package.json')).get('scripts',{}); sys.exit(0 if 'lint' in s and 'format' in s else 1)"

assertions.text: Uses pnpm for install commands, matching the lockfile and packageManager field
assertions.script: grep -qE 'pnpm (add|install)' output.md && ! grep -qE '\bnpm install --save-dev\b|\byarn add\b' output.md

evals.name: eslint-oxfmt-no-prettier-files
evals.prompt: Our TypeScript project has no formatting set up yet. We want ESLint for linting and oxfmt for formatting. We use npm. Apply the changes directly, you have my go-ahead, please don't stop to ask me to confirm.
evals.expected_output: Creates eslint.config.js and .oxfmtrc.json, adds eslint-config-prettier to disable ESLint's formatting rules and places it last in the ESLint config, and adds lint and format scripts. Critically it creates no .prettierrc.json and no .prettierignore: eslint-config-prettier is only a compatibility shim, and Prettier was never selected as the formatter.

assertions.text: Does not create .prettierignore
Does not create .prettierrc.json or any other Prettier config
Creates .oxfmtrc.json
Creates eslint.config.js
Adds eslint-config-prettier for ESLint and formatter compatibility
Places the eslint-config-prettier entry last in eslint.config.js, where it can actually override the formatting rules
The format script runs oxfmt, not prettier
assertions.script: python3 -c "import json,sys; s=json.load(open('sandbox/package.json')).get('scripts',{}); f=s.get('format',''); sys.exit(0 if 'oxfmt' in f and 'prettier' not in f else 1)"

evals.name: switch-prettier-to-oxfmt
evals.prompt: We're moving from Prettier to oxfmt for formatting. Remove Prettier and replace it with oxfmt. Keep ESLint as-is. We use npm. Apply the changes directly, you have my go-ahead, please don't stop to ask me to confirm.
evals.expected_output: Creates .oxfmtrc.json, removes prettier from devDependencies, deletes the now-orphaned .prettierrc.json, repoints the format script at oxfmt, and keeps eslint-config-prettier wired in so ESLint's formatting rules stay disabled under the new formatter. It does not create .prettierignore, which would be a Prettier artefact in a project that just dropped Prettier.

assertions.text: Does not create .prettierignore
Creates .oxfmtrc.json
Removes the prettier dependency, while keeping the eslint-config-prettier shim
assertions.script: python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(open('sandbox/package.json')).get('devDependencies',{}); sys.exit(0 if 'prettier' not in d else 1)"

assertions.text: The format script runs oxfmt rather than prettier
assertions.script: python3 -c "import json,sys; s=json.load(open('sandbox/package.json')).get('scripts',{}); f=s.get('format',''); sys.exit(0 if 'oxfmt' in f and 'prettier' not in f else 1)"

assertions.text: Keeps eslint-config-prettier present, since ESLint's formatting rules still need disabling under oxfmt
Removes the orphaned .prettierrc.json rather than leaving dead config behind
Leaves the ESLint rule set itself alone, the user having asked to keep ESLint as-is
